title: Joining Piron's band, the Country Club and the Streckfus boat
summary: Leo Dejan recruits him for Piron's band at the New Orleans Country Club; Captain Streckfus then hires the band for the boat in 1933.

story.theme_name: Dance halls, lake camps and riverboat bandstands
story.community_name: Working the Streckfus riverboats with Fate Marable

blocks.x: I was staying on La Hop, La Hop and La Prusse, I believe it was, and Randy was staying right across the street from me. So, well like I said, at that time in working with the big band, I'd always work with some guys with maybe two or three pieces like Ryan Young and Frank's Quarter when the big band wasn't doing nothing. And I was doing a little range in that time for the band. Yeah. So when the word got around and Sidney had let me go, well, I remember Leo Dazio came to my house because he had one of the guys that had recommended me highly, see, in the band. So he asked me would I join them because he had heard that I wasn't with Sidney. I said, well, yes, you know. And they were working out at the Orange Country Club. They had three nights out there a week. I remember it was Friday, Saturday, and Sunday evening. Well, that was pretty good money, you know, as of now to a day. So I went to rehearsal. They were rehearsing on Ivor Street at the Piano Playhouse. His name was Alla Greta.

Yeah, he was arranging for the band. And in the band I remember well, there was Peter On the Leader, a violin player. The sax section was Arthur Durbin, Elliot Taylor, and Joe Ruzon. Elliot Taylor played Clannett in sax at that time. It was very good. I think Arthur Durbin was the first sax and he did a little singing. And in the rhythm section were Alla Greta on piano. He was very young. He was one of the young fellas. And Alfred William was on drums, Simon Moreau on bass, and me on banjo. I was playing banjo and guitar. Oh, yeah. So I remember well in playing at the New Orleans Country Club, Mr. Crawford Ellis, I believe he was president of something like that. He was the one that got Peter on the band. And I remember one thing was on a Saturday night. Captain Boyne and his wife were out there. Well, I knew the captain, you know. And he came over and spoke to the band. He recognized me. And that's how we got the job on the boat.

Oh, that was in, let's see, about around 33. 33, yeah. So I remember Captain Boyne came over and talked to Peter on and told him he wanted to come down to the office and see him. You know, he said he'd like to have his band and he'd like to have him on the boat. And he spoke to me and he said, yeah, I said, that's sales. He said, sales have worked for us, which I had already worked with Pete Marvillin and sitting in there's being banned on the boat. So Peter on asked me about it. I told him, I said, well, that's a good job. I said, he said, well, I do. Tip Captain Boyan Strecker had requested that Peter Bogart would take charge of the band, because like I said, the young fellas in there, like I was up in the East, and Booker was living there, but I mean, they just thought they would look too young to have, because Eddie Pearson wanted to take charge, but they wouldn't let him take charge, see. So Peter Bogart was lead, I think Eddie Pearson was sort of a manager, like, see. So I really missed Peter on that particular year, and we, that particular year we closed, we usually come back here, but we closed in St. Louis, and I remember it was the last week in August, if I remember right, and I stayed around St. Louis about a week or so, and I had a person, a very good friend of mine, had lived in Chicago, and he used to always ask me to come up there, you see, so I thought that was a fine time for me to go up there and see him, and then...
